notable_absence.finding: 'Each user is associated with one or more _roles_, which permit limited access-privileges' names the RBAC mechanism in passing for a fourth time in this batch, again without naming a specific role. This page's own content (password strength, master password, community-edition user cap) is entirely about USER lifecycle, never about which role is needed to perform any of the administrative actions it describes (setting password policy, force-password-change, resetting the admin password) - the same gap noted on authentication-overview.json, now confirmed a third time on a page whose subject (users) is directly adjacent to RBAC's subject (roles).

cross_component_finding: The default password policy is stated as extremely weak ('demands only that the password have a minimum of six characters') immediately followed by a strong recommendation to strengthen it for production - the same soft-default-plus-warning pattern documented for SCRAM-SHA1 on authentication-overview.json ('it is recommended to disable SCRAM-SHA1 unless it is absolutely required'). Two independent pages in this batch document a secure-by-configuration rather than secure-by-default posture for different parts of the same authentication subsystem.
cross_product_finding: No equivalent of Community Edition's 20-user cap (server:user behavesDifferentlyUnder edition:community) exists anywhere in the promoted registry's Capella material - Capella has no Community/Enterprise edition split at all (its own axis is deployment:capella vs. on-prem editions, per the registry note on deployment:capella), so this is a genuinely Server-only constraint with no cross-product analogue to compare against, reinforcing edition-gating as an axis that is meaningful for Server and structurally absent for Capella.
